overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by not taking roll call votes with a remote member and by omitting a procedural vote from the minutes, but not for the minutes' brief remarks.

allegations.summary: Board did not take roll call votes at its May 28 meeting even though one member attended remotely.
allegations.key_passage: The Board acknowledges that it failed to conduct votes by roll call at the May 28 Meeting, which Member Simon attended remotely.

allegations.summary: May 28 minutes omitted the Board's formal vote to take agenda items out of order.
allegations.key_passage: Although this vote was not on a substantive matter, and merely concerned the order of topics to be discussed, it was a formal vote that should have been included within the minutes.

allegations.summary: May 28 minutes allegedly lacked a summary of the chair and member remarks about reconnecting the remote member.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find the minutes insufficiently detailed for failure to include a summary of these brief remarks.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued the violations were not discoverable within 30 days; the Board did not contest timeliness.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we assume without finding that the complaint was timely filed with the Board.

remedy: Amend the May 28 minutes to reflect the vote to discuss topics out of order, within 60 days of the letter.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to amend the minutes to reflect this vote within 60 day of the date of this letter. We also order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
